html:
William Walker was an American adventurer who invaded Nicaragua in 1855 with a small private army and made himself its president in 1856. He was driven out in 1857 and shot in Honduras in 1860.

Such men were called filibusters. Walker came at the invitation of the Liberal party of León, which was at war with the Conservatives of Granada. He took Granada, seized the transit company and, as president, legalised slavery to win support in the American South.

The other Central American states, led by Costa Rica, went to war against him, with the Conservatives of Nicaragua. His men lost at San Jacinto and Rivas, and burned Granada as they retreated. He surrendered in 1857. On a later raid he was caught and executed at Trujillo, Honduras. He is remembered as a symbol of American interference.
sum: William Walker was an American adventurer who invaded Nicaragua in 1855 with a small private army and made himself its president in 1856. He was driven out in 1857 and shot in Honduras in 1860.
